And in the same year there was a famine in Baghdad,
and a kor of wheat was sold for ninety gold dinars;
and many locusts were seen in the region of Mosul.
And shortly afterwards Nikephoros, the king of the Romans, came,
and encamped against Antioch.
And from there he went to Tripoli,
and burned all the buildings outside the city.
And he went and captured the strong fortress of Gaza,
and took immense plunder from it.
And he came and encamped midway between Homs and Aleppo,
and stayed for two months, taking captives and plundering;
and there was no one who could confront him.
One hundred thousand young male and female captives were numbered with him,
for he took neither an old man nor an old woman,
except that some of them they killed {OCR?},
and some of them he released.
And were it not for a discord that fell among the Romans,
he would also have captured Aleppo and Antioch.
And his face was set toward Jerusalem,
yet he was unable to go,
because those with him grew weary and disgusted {OCR?} from the immense slaughter they had committed,
and from the heavy weight of the booty they had taken.
And in the year one thousand two hundred and eighty-one,
1281 of the Greeks,
(970 of our Lord),
which is the year three hundred and fifty-nine,
359 of the Arabs,
the Romans hatched a plot with the Christians of the fortress of Luqa, which is in the vicinity of Antioch,
that they should enter Antioch
and pretend that they were afraid of the Romans and had fled,
and stay in it until the Roman army should come against Antioch,
and lend a hand from within in opening the city.
And when they had done so,
after two months the brother of King Nikephoros arrived with forty thousand Romans,
and they surrounded the wall of Antioch.
And the people of the fortress of Luqa gave them a hand from the side of the mountain,
and the Romans entered Antioch and captured it.
And after the great slaughter they committed,
they separated the old men and old women and those of small stature, and said to them:
"Go wherever you wish."
And they took young men and maidens and children, more than twenty thousand souls,
and sent them to the land of the Romans.
And they also sent ten thousand horsemen to Aleppo,
and the people of Aleppo undertook to pay tribute to the Romans every year of a specified amount,
and they took from them eight hostages and departed.
